summary: Phase 149O.20J.2 -- Class-B Deployment Verifier Narrow Defect Repair Independent Verification: independent repair-verification only, no production source/contract/script file modified, no repair performed. Independently reconstructed 149O.20J.1's own production diff (git diff 0f2bb93c^ 0f2bb93c, confirming the pre-repair baseline commit is dce667e7), confirming it touches exactly hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py and hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py with zero unrelated hunks, and that hatp_class_b_conformance.py is byte-unchanged. J-1: read the real running interpreter's site.addpackage() source directly (CPython 3.14.5, not inferred from prose), independently reconstructed the historical predicate from dce667e7's actual source, proved it misses the tab-delimited import\t form (and over-flags a leading-whitespace import line) against a 17-case adversarial matrix derived from the independently-confirmed CPython rule, directly executed a scratch .pth fixture through real site.addpackage() to prove CPython does execute the tab form, then confirmed the repaired _pth_line_is_executable matches the CPython rule with zero mismatches across the same matrix, plus a full _check_pth_files comment/safe-path/tab-import/writable-file matrix exercised via monkeypatched fixtures. J-2: reconstructed the historical _current_agent_identity from dce667e7's actual source, confirmed it omits os.getegid(), ran the effective-group matrix (getgroups=[10,20]/getegid=30, getgroups=[10,20,30]/getegid=30, getgroups=[]/getegid=30) against the live repaired function (all three correct), confirmed dedup/set semantics, confirmed the source uses os.getegid() not os.getgid(), and ran the decisive isolated-channel permission attack (target group=30, mode 0o060, ACL sub-check forced to report none so only the mode+group channel is exercised): historical group set {10,20} -> write=False (would incorrectly pass as no-write-access); repaired group set {10,20,30} -> write=True, reason=agent_group_membership_grants_write (correctly detects the write authority). J-3: confirmed from dce667e7's actual source that historical _check_trusted_git calls the ACL-blind _resolve_trusted_executable primitive directly; reproduced the blindness live by simulating an ACL-only write grant on a mode-safe git fixture and confirming the historical primitive still resolves it as trusted; confirmed the repaired _resolve_trusted_executable_with_effective_access wrapper rejects git-executable ACL-only grants, immediate-parent ACL-only grants, PATH-preceding agent-writable directories, and ACL-tool-indeterminate results (fail-closed, never interpreted as no-ACL), while the pre-existing fake-Git-via-hostile-PATH regression stays rejected; proved non-recursion both statically (AST call-graph search across all relevant functions found no path cycling back to the wrapper) and dynamically (a re-entrancy poison test monkeypatched the wrapper to raise on re-entry and directly exercised the real ACL branch's own getfacl/ls tool resolution -- the poisoned wrapper's call counter stayed at 0 throughout); confirmed the ACL evidence mechanism (external getfacl on Linux / ls -lde on macOS, resolved via the same narrow non-recursive PATH walk, itself checked only by mode+group by deliberate, disclosed design to avoid recursion); confirmed topology and Git share the identical _effective_write_access/_ancestor_chain_safe primitives (no divergent policy) and that Git decisions use the same repaired, centralized _current_agent_identity(). One pre-existing, already-disclosed, non-blocking observation recorded (not a J-1/J-2/J-3 regression and not new): the shared, unmodified _ancestor_chain_safe primitive stops its upward walk at the first ancestor proven non-writable rather than continuing to a true root boundary, so a writable grandparent directory behind an already-safe immediate parent is not examined by the resolution -- this exact scenario was already independently constructed and disclosed by 149O.20J's own frozen suite (test_deep_ancestor_writable_beyond_immediate_parent_is_caught, whose docstring documents the stop-at-first-safe-boundary design as intended), is unmodified by 149O.20J.1's repair, and applies identically (not divergently) to Protected Root's own HBDC-REQ-017 check via the same shared primitive -- outside this narrow repair's three-named-defect scope; recommend a future phase re-examine HBDC-REQ-017's exact reading. Verdict: J-1/J-2/J-3 all INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED at the non-authoritative verifier-implementation boundary (HMIC source-scope binding and readiness/certification consumption remain separately gated, not performed or authorized by this phase). Created a new 56-test independent verification module, tests/test_phase_149o_20j_2_class_b_deployment_verifier_narrow_defect_repair_independent_verification.py: 56/56 passed. Historical-defect assertions read the pre-repair source directly via git show dce667e7:<path> (never an inlined copy); live-repair assertions call the current production functions directly, never importing 149O.20J or 149O.20J.1's own test constants/helpers as oracle. One test's own first draft (the deep-ancestor observation test) initially asserted the wrong outcome because its PATH fixture excluded a real ls/getfacl resolution path, causing the ACL sub-check to report indeterminate rather than a genuine safe boundary and masking the actual behavior under test; corrected to include a real system bin directory on PATH so the ACL tool resolves for real, reproducing the same result independently confirmed by manual inspection. Regression-only reruns (not independent proof): 149O.20J.1's own suite 26/26 passed; 149O.20J's own frozen suite 61 passed/1 skipped (pre-existing)/1 disclosed-expected failure unchanged from 149O.20J.1's own citation (test_agent_effective_gid_not_in_getgroups_can_be_missed, a finding-confirmation test superseded now that the gap it documented is closed, per its own docstring, left unmodified per historical-snapshot-preservation discipline); 149O.20I suites 98/98 passed; 149O.20H suite 21/21 passed. Broad sweep (pytest -k 'class_b or hbdc or hmic or 149o_20', -n auto): 45 failed/1188 passed/5 skipped/1 error; independently confirmed via git stash -u comparison that the exact same 45 failed/5 skipped/1 error persists with this phase's two new files removed (only the passed count differs, by exactly this phase's own 56 new tests) -- zero new failures attributable to this phase. Fast Green (-m fast_green -n auto): approximately 70-71 failed/6744-6745 passed/5 skipped/1 error across repeated runs, a +/-1 delta consistent with known pytest-xdist worker-count/collection-order variance rather than a new failure -- directly confirmed none of this phase's 56 new tests appear in either run's failure list, and the failure set's content matches the pre-existing debt category (dirty-tree snapshot checks tied to historical commit ranges, pinned requirement/attack-count assertions from older 149O.19.x HMIC phases, the pre-existing fido2-import collection error, and the one disclosed 20J regression). Real-host result invoked read-only against the live conformance aggregator: NON_COMPLIANT (not COMPLIANT, expected on this unprovisioned host), before/after git status --short byte-identical confirming zero mutation. Zero production authority consumers of the three verifier modules reconfirmed via repository-wide search (zero matches outside the three modules themselves, and individually reconfirmed absent from hatp_mandatory_cutover.py, hatp_mandatory_certification.py, scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py, permission_broker.py, hatp_rollback_consumption.py). Fresh extraction of the live _FROZEN_AUTHORITY_BEARING_FILES constant from hatp_mandatory_certification.py confirms exactly 25 entries, none of the three verifier module names present. Status vocabulary (6-member closed set, COMPLIANT sole positive), public zero-parameter/neutral-locator signatures, and fail-closed aggregation (all-satisfied yields COMPLIANT, any single failure does not) all independently reconfirmed unchanged. Both of 149O.20I's own self-caught fixes (sys.meta_path class-vs-instance handling; HBDC-REQ-004 environ/PATH admin-inference false-positive narrowing) re-attacked directly and confirmed preserved. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20J_2_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_VERIFIER_NARROW_DEFECT_REPAIR_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md documenting the baseline, diff reconstruction, historical reproduction and CPython-semantics derivation for all three findings, live repair verification, the non-blocking ancestor-walk observation, cross-cutting read-only/consumer/HMIC-scope verification, regression results, governance close checks, findings, exit status, CBV-S1/CBV-S10, verification verdict, and recommended next phase. Updated PROJECT_STATUS.md (demoting 149O.20J.1 to a new stacked Previous Phase entry) and CHANGELOG.md. CBV-S1: VERIFIER IMPLEMENTATION INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- HMIC SOURCE-SCOPE BINDING REQUIRED NEXT -- NOT CLOSED. CBV-S10: unchanged, still NOT CLOSED. Class-B remains CONTRACT VERIFIED -- VERIFIER IMPLEMENTATION INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. This phase does not authorize real provisioning, certification, activation, HMIC scope evolution, or readiness integration. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20K -- HMIC Class-B Verifier Source-Scope Contract Evolution -- not authorized by this phase.
